title: Portable Driver Triage — findings.json
description: Written by the AI into reports/<sha256>/<run_id>/findings.json as the deliverable of a Mode A or Mode B deep analysis of one bundle. Companion findings.md is a human-readable rendering of the same content and is not schematized.

driver_sha256.description: Must match the sha256 of the driver this bundle analyzes. The AI copies it from identity.json / the per-bundle AGENTS.md, never invents it.

scope.description: Active scope profile for this analysis. Must match the scope the bundle was produced under.

agent.description: Model identifier that produced this document, e.g. claude-opus-4-7, gpt-5, local-llama-70b. Free-form; used for provenance, not validation.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC, must end with Z.

findings.description: Findings inside the active scope. Empty array is valid (the AI analyzed and found nothing in-scope that meets the citation bar).

out_of_scope.description: Observations the AI considers worth surfacing but which fall outside the active scope profile. Same shape as findings. Never promote one of these into findings.

unknowns.description: Things the bundle did not let the AI resolve. One short line each. Keeps the operator aware of gaps instead of letting the AI silently drop them.

id.description: F-001, F-002, … Zero-padded, monotonic within the document.

title.description: Short, imperative, factual. No clickbait, no severity words baked into the title.

class.description: Closed vocabulary. If none fit, use 'other' and explain in notes_for_human. New classes require a schema_version bump.

confidence.description: CONFIRMED: traced end-to-end through pseudo-C and (where applicable) verified in disasm_full.txt. PLAUSIBLE: pattern/heuristic matched (clone, missing probe, dangerous import reachable) but the path was not fully traced in-bundle.

severity_in_scope.description: Severity relative to the active scope. A critical input-injection finding may be unrelated to the stakes of an arbitrary-memory scope and vice versa.

ioctl.description: IOCTL code the finding is anchored to. Null when the finding is driver-wide rather than per-IOCTL.

handler.description: Function address of the handler. Null when the finding is not located in a specific function.

method.description: IOCTL buffering method for the handler. Null when ioctl is null or the method could not be resolved.

call_chain.description: At least one citation. Every entry must point to a file inside the bundle and a line that actually contains the referenced construct. The whole document is rejected if any finding has an empty call_chain.

file.description: Path relative to the bundle directory (where findings.json lives). Shared L1/L2 artifacts are reached via ../ (e.g., ../disasm_full.txt). Run-local artifacts are relative (e.g., l3_decomp/0x14000b1c0.c).

note.description: One short sentence stating what the cited line shows.

primitive.description: One or two sentences stating the capability granted by the finding, in operational terms (what the caller controls, what the driver does with it, what the result is). Never a weaponization recipe.

clone_evidence.description: Clone-detection evidence tying this finding to a known-vulnerable driver. Null when the finding is independent of any clone hit.

ref.description: CVE id when available (preferred when the match corresponds to one), otherwise the ref_id from the clone_hits entry in the bundle, or null.

source.description: Path + anchor into the clone evidence file, e.g. l3_decomp/clones.json#ene_sys

detection_ideas.description: Free-form strings. Each one a concrete detection suggestion a defender could implement (YARA rule hint, EDR signal, Sigma rule sketch, oncall query, …). Keep each item one line.

notes_for_human.description: Optional. Omit the field entirely if nothing to add. Use for caveats, decompiler artifacts worth flagging, or ambiguities the operator should know about.
